title: Beyond Content: How Grammatical Gender Shapes Visual Representation in Text-to-Image Models

bias_targets.methodology: The study evaluates gender representation (male vs. female) in images generated by Text-to-Image models (DALL-E 3, Ideogram v3, Flux Pro 1.1) using the GRAMVIS benchmark. It classifies the gender of persons in generated images to determine if grammatical gender markers (e.g., masculine/feminine articles) influence the visual gender of the subject, particularly when the grammatical gender contradicts the stereotypical gender of the concept (gender-divergent words).

The paper investigates how language structure (specifically grammatical gender) and language resource availability (high-resource vs. medium-resource languages) shape visual outputs. It compares effects across five gendered languages (French, Spanish, German, Italian, Russian) and two gender-neutral control languages (English, Chinese) to isolate the influence of linguistic features on generated content.

The researchers categorize gender-divergent words into five social dimensions (occupation, personal traits, power dynamics, social status, relations) to analyze how grammatical gender interacts with and potentially overrides semantic gender stereotypes in visual generation.
